steps.u: Review the migration file in this PR for the users table. We have 40 million rows.

steps.r:
class AddPlanToUsers < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.1]
  def change
    add_column :users, :plan, :string, null: false, default: 'free'
    add_index :users, :plan
  end
end

steps.a: On Postgres 11 or later, adding a column with a constant default is metadata only, so the add_column itself is cheap. The index is the problem: add_index without algorithm: :concurrently takes a lock that blocks writes to users while it builds, which on 40 million rows could take minutes.

Postgres 15 is confirmed, so the column add is fine. My requests: use add_index with algorithm: :concurrently and disable_ddl_transaction!, and consider whether an index on a three-value column is useful at all, since a low-cardinality index is rarely chosen by the planner. I did not edit the file.

reference.summary: Reviewed a migration adding a plan column and index to a 40 million row users table. The column with a constant default is cheap on Postgres 15, but the index is built without concurrency and would block writes, so the review asks for a concurrent build and questions whether an index on so few distinct values is useful. Nothing was edited.
facts: add_column with constant default is metadata only on Postgres 11+
index created without algorithm concurrently would lock writes
specific: migration safety on a large table
